name: The Overthinker's Flowchart
why_it_works: Everyone has stalled on booking something for months. A flowchart that loops viewers back to the start no matter what they answer is relatable exaggeration: they see their own procrastination drawn out and laugh at themselves. The exit from the loop is the easiest possible first step, so the CTA feels like relief, not pressure.

hook.pattern: Pose the yes/no question your audience has been avoiding, in flowchart form.
examples: Should I finally book {{service}}? A flowchart.
The official flowchart for putting off {{service}}.
Thinking about {{service}}? Follow the arrows. Good luck.

slides.headline: Should I finally book {{service}}?
slides.body: A scientific flowchart. Start at the top. Be honest.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 hand-drawn whiteboard flowchart aesthetic, marker lines, one START box at top with the question, {{brand}} accent color arrows, off-white board texture

slides.headline: Have you been meaning to?
slides.body: YES: go to the next slide. NO: you're on slide two, so yes.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 marker-drawn decision diamond with YES and NO arrows that both curve the same direction, whiteboard texture, playful

slides.headline: Then you thought…
slides.body: "{{stall_excuse_1}}" Arrow points to the next box.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 marker-drawn box with a thought bubble, small doodle of a calendar with pages flying off, whiteboard texture

slides.headline: Then you planned…
slides.body: "{{stall_excuse_2}}" Arrow points to the next box.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 marker-drawn box with an elaborate scribbled plan, tiny doodled stick figure looking determined, whiteboard texture

slides.headline: Decision box
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 oversized marker-drawn decision diamond crammed with tiny doodles of a phone, stars and a magic 8-ball, arrows tangled around it, whiteboard

slides.headline: Return to slide one.
slides.body: Every arrow goes back to the start. Ask us how we know.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 whiteboard flowchart where every arrow loops back to the START box, a single big red marker circle around the loop, comic tone

slides.headline: Or skip the chart entirely
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 the whiteboard has been erased except one clean marker arrow pointing off the board to a bright {{brand}} booking button drawn in brand color

slides.headline: {{brand}}: exit the loop
slides.body: No judgment about how long it's been. We mean it. {{disclosure}}
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 warm candid photo of a smiling {{brand}} front desk team member, welcoming gesture, bright clean light, brand colors visible

craft.technique: Relatable exaggeration in a looping flowchart (circular structure)
craft.notes: Setup: a fake-scientific flowchart and an honest yes/no question; the 'NO' arrow already points to the same place as 'YES', the first small laugh. Escalation: two stall excuses the viewer has actually thought, then an absurd decision box that pushes it into ridiculous territory. Turn: 'Return to slide one': the reveal that every path loops, which is the core joke about our own procrastination. Tag: 'Ask us how we know' admits the brand team does it too (punching at self), then the clean exit arrow. Timing in a carousel: the loop slide must be a hard visual surprise, so keep slides two to five visually busy and make the loop slide one big red circle; the swipe before it is the pause.

do_not: Shame people for how long they've waited; the joke is on everyone, including the team
Use fear, pain or health scares as the stall excuses
Make the exit step anything harder than one tap or one call
Add a branch that implies a medical or financial outcome
compliance: Dental: no promises of 'painless' or specific results; no clinical claims in any flowchart box
Med spa: no before/after images or result claims; any treatment named must be described as performed by licensed providers; add 'results vary' if a treatment is named
Real estate: include brokerage name and license number where your state requires; no wording about who a neighborhood is 'for' (fair housing)
Life coach: no income, health or life-outcome promises in the exit step
